newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bordeaux wine exports rise despite nuclear boycott.
newsitem.headline: Bordeaux wine exports rise despite nuclear boycott.

text.p: Exports of Bordeaux wines rose by two percent in volume and 13 percent in value during the 1995-1996 season despite the effects of a north European consumer boycott against French nuclear weapons tests.

The CIVB Bordeaux wine industry body said on Wednesday that between September 1, 1995 and August 31, 1996, some 1.874 billion hectolitres of wine had been exported with a value of 4.85 billion francs.
Red Bordeaux wines were up six percent in volume and 16 percent in value while white wines registered a decline of nine percent in volume and three percent in value.

The effects of the nuclear test boycott were most clearly felt in sales to north European countries, CIVB said. Exports to Norway fell 34 percent in volume, in Denmark they were down by 30 percent and in Sweden the plunge was 56 percent.
The CIVB said that the lost sales were compenstated by good exports to other European Union markets and sales rises in Switzerland and in particular Japan and south east Asia.
